subject: Data Structures
content: An array is a linear data structure that stores elements of the same data type in contiguous memory locations. Arrays allow constant-time access using index positions and are the foundation for many other data structures.

subject: Data Structures
content: A linked list is a dynamic data structure where each node stores data and a reference to the next node. Unlike arrays linked lists do not require contiguous memory and allow efficient insertion and deletion operations.

subject: Data Structures
content: A binary tree is a hierarchical data structure in which each node has at most two children referred to as the left child and the right child. Binary trees are used in searching sorting and expression parsing.

subject: Data Structures
content: A stack is a last-in first-out data structure used in function calls and expression evaluation. A queue is a first-in first-out structure used in scheduling and breadth-first search algorithms.

subject: Database Management
content: SQL stands for Structured Query Language and is used to manage relational databases. Core commands include SELECT INSERT UPDATE and DELETE. SQL uses tables with rows and columns to organize data efficiently.

subject: Database Management
content: Database normalization is the process of organizing tables to reduce redundancy and improve data integrity. Normal forms from 1NF to BCNF define rules for structuring data to avoid anomalies during insertion deletion and update.

subject: Database Management
content: An index is a database object that speeds up query performance by creating a pointer to data in a table. Indexing reduces full table scans but adds overhead to write operations.

subject: Machine Learning
content: Linear regression is a supervised learning algorithm that predicts a continuous output variable based on one or more input features. The model finds the best-fit line by minimizing the mean squared error between predicted and actual values.

subject: Machine Learning
content: Classification is a supervised learning task that assigns data points to predefined categories. Common algorithms include logistic regression decision trees and support vector machines. Evaluation metrics include accuracy precision recall and F1 score.

subject: Machine Learning
content: Clustering is an unsupervised learning technique that groups similar data points together without predefined labels. K-means clustering assigns each point to the nearest cluster centroid and iterates until convergence.

subject: Python Programming
content: A function in Python is a reusable block of code that performs a specific task. Functions are defined using the def keyword and can accept parameters and return values. Functions improve code modularity and readability.

subject: Python Programming
content: Object-oriented programming in Python uses classes and objects to model real-world entities. Key concepts include encapsulation inheritance polymorphism and abstraction. Classes define blueprints and objects are instances of those classes.

subject: Python Programming
content: Python allows reading and writing files using the open function with modes r for read w for write and a for append. Context managers with the with statement ensure files are properly closed after operations.

subject: Data Science
content: Data visualization converts raw data into graphical representations to identify patterns and trends. Popular Python libraries include Matplotlib for basic plots Seaborn for statistical visuals and Plotly for interactive charts.

subject: Data Science
content: Feature engineering is the process of transforming raw data into meaningful features that improve machine learning model performance. Techniques include normalization encoding categorical variables handling missing values and creating new derived features.
